title: Mage Wars

basic.title: First Game Flow: Read, Prepare, Resolve
basic.description: Start with the win condition, mage readouts, channeling, and planning, then continue through summoning, public discard, the quickcast window, movement, walls, and guarding.

steps.intro: Mage Wars lasts several rounds, until one mage has taken enough damage to be destroyed. The last mage standing wins the game.
steps.selfHud: Your mage panel shows life, damage, mana, channeling, action marker, and quickcast marker. Apprentice mages start with Life 24, Mana 10, and Channeling 10; your goal is to deal enough damage to defeat the opposing mage.
steps.opponentHud: The opponent panel shows the same readouts. Opponent prepared spells use card backs and a count, so card names stay hidden until revealed.
steps.stage: Each round moves through Reset, Channel, Upkeep, Planning, Deployment, Initiative Quickcast, Creature Action, and Final Quickcast. Reset, Channel, and Upkeep with no pending choice resolve automatically; during Planning, prepare 0 to 2 spells, or use “Skip spell preparation” to submit an empty plan. Deployment and both quickcast windows then resolve in order, with creature movement or attacks during Creature Action.
steps.channelResult: The Beastmaster currently has Channeling 10; after channeling, the mana supply gains 10 mana.
steps.preparePlanning: Upkeep is resolving before planning begins.
steps.spellCardReading: Use this spell-card legend first: cost, action, range, target, type, school, and level determine how you prepare and cast.
steps.planningSkip: Planning allows 0 to 2 prepared spells. An empty plan means preparing no spells this round; on the normal table, “Skip spell preparation” submits it, and both players enter Deployment after the other mage finishes planning. This tutorial prepares two spells next.
steps.attackBarReading: Jungle Wolf is in your prepared spells and is about to be cast. Read its attack bar first: the left icons tell quick or full action and melee or ranged attack; the right side shows range, damage type, attack dice, extra effects, and traits. Click Next when done.
steps.planCreatureNextPage: Click the next page to find Jungle Wolf.
steps.planSelectWolf: Jungle Wolf is a Creature spell: it summons a creature into the arena to keep fighting. Click the Jungle Wolf card body to put it into the first prepared slot.
steps.planIncantationNextPage: Click the next page to find Rouse the Beast.
steps.planSelectRouse: Rouse the Beast is an Incantation spell: it resolves a one-time text effect, then goes to your discard pile. Click the Rouse the Beast card body to put it into the second prepared slot.
steps.planConfirm: Click “Confirm prep 2/2” to submit this round's plan.
steps.prepareOpponentSpells: The opponent prepares spells through the formal flow; they stay card backs until revealed.
steps.preparedAndHidden: Both players choose their own spells at the same time. Your chosen spells are kept hidden from the opponent so they cannot know your plan.
steps.deploySelectWolf: Click Jungle Wolf in your prepared spells.
steps.wolfSummoned: Jungle Wolf has been summoned into the Beastmaster's zone. It enters without a ready action, so the spent action marker means it cannot act yet. This is a reading step: do not click the wolf yet, click Next to continue.
steps.rouseSelectSpell: Click Rouse the Beast in your prepared spells.
steps.rouseTargetWolf: Click the Jungle Wolf card body in the arena so Rouse the Beast targets it.
steps.passYourDeployment: Jungle Wolf's action marker is ready, but this is still the deployment phase. Click “End deployment” first; after the action phase begins, click the Jungle Wolf card body to move it.
steps.opponentDeploymentResults: The opponent's deployment and one public attack spell are resolving through the formal flow.
steps.opponentPublicView: The opponent has resolved deployment and one public attack spell. Click the eye in the opponent panel's upper-left corner to switch to the opponent public view; this only reads public information and does not let you act for the opponent.
steps.discardReading: The same discard area now shows the opponent's public discard: resolved opponent spells stay here face up. Unrevealed prepared spells still remain card backs.
steps.backToSelfView: After reading the opponent's discard, click “Back to your view” to return to your spellbook, prepared spells, and next action.
steps.opponentPassDeployment: After the opponent finishes deployment, both players enter the initiative quickcast window. Quickcast is a rule timing window, not a response and not always-on free casting; now you decide whether to use a quick spell.
steps.skipInitiativeQuickcast: This is your initiative quickcast window. Quickcast is only available when the rules open this window; you are not casting now, so click “Pass quickcast”.
steps.opponentPassInitiativeQuickcast: The opponent also passes initiative quickcast, so your creature action begins. Next, use Jungle Wolf to move.
steps.moveSelectWolf: Click the Jungle Wolf card body in the arena to choose it as the moving creature.
steps.moveTargetZone: Click an adjacent zone to move.
steps.endCreatureAction: Moving has used the wolf's action. Click “End action” so both players finish Creature Action and enter Final Quickcast.
steps.opponentPassCreatureAction: The opponent's Creature Action resolves through the formal flow.
steps.skipFinalQuickcast: This is your Final Quickcast window. You are not casting a quick spell now, so click “Pass quickcast”.
steps.roundTwoPlanning: The new round's Reset, Channel, and Upkeep have resolved automatically; Jungle Wolf's action marker is ready again. Prepare Wall of Thorns this round and see how a wall occupies the edge between two zones.
steps.planWallNextPage: Click the next page to find Wall of Thorns.
steps.planSelectThornsWall: Wall of Thorns is a Wall spell: it is placed on the edge between two adjacent zones. Click the Wall of Thorns card body to put it into the prepared slot.
steps.planConfirmThornsWall: Click “Confirm prep 1/2” to submit this round's plan.
steps.prepareOpponentEmptyPlan: The opponent prepares no spells this round, so both players enter Deployment.
steps.opponentPassSecondDeployment: The opponent passes Deployment first, so it is your turn to cast the prepared Wall spell.
steps.wallPrepared: Wall of Thorns is in your prepared spells. A Wall spell does not summon into a zone; it targets the edge between two zones.
steps.wallSelectSpell: Click Wall of Thorns in your prepared spells.
steps.wallTargetEdge: Click the edge between the Beastmaster's zone and the zone to its right.
steps.wallCardResult: Wall of Thorns is now attached to that edge, shown by its own spell card rather than a normal creature slot.
steps.wallEffectReading: This wall blocks movement and line of sight across the edge; later attacks or spells must check whether the wall lies between source and target.
steps.endSecondDeployment: The wall has been deployed. Click “End deployment” to enter the initiative quickcast window.
steps.opponentPassSecondInitiativeQuickcast: The opponent passes initiative quickcast, so now you decide whether to quickcast.
steps.skipSecondInitiativeQuickcast: You are still not using quickcast this round, so click “Pass quickcast”.
steps.opponentPassSecondCreatureAction: The opponent passes Creature Action, so Jungle Wolf can act now.
steps.guardSelectWolf: Click the Jungle Wolf card body in the arena to choose it as this action's source.
steps.guardAction: Click “Guard” in the action dock. Guard is the action; the guard marker appears on the unit after it resolves.
steps.guardTokenResult: Jungle Wolf gains the guard marker and spends its action for the round. The marker stays on the unit to show it protects friendly objects in the same zone.
steps.endSecondCreatureAction: Guarding has spent Jungle Wolf's action. Click “End action” to enter Final Quickcast.
steps.opponentPassSecondFinalQuickcast: The opponent passes Final Quickcast, so it is your turn to close the round.
steps.finish: You have now gone through Reset, Channel, Upkeep, Planning, Deployment, Initiative Quickcast, Creature Action, and Final Quickcast, while reading the board and cards, summoning Jungle Wolf, checking public discard, moving a creature, casting a wall, and guarding with a unit.
